deepdive.sec: Banking — Private Sector Bank (mid-cap, turnaround; SMBC-sponsored)

bull_bear.body: - 6 years without a dividend; shareholder pushback on dilution acknowledged. Enabling INR 16,000 cr resolution is a refresh of last year's — optionality, not a trigger; would raise near 13% CET-1 to match peer buffers, not from need. Priority is compounding core ROA/ROE before any raise; DTA aids capital efficiency.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **ROE still ~8.3%** — below cost of equity; re-rating needs the core-ROA climb to stick.
- **Dilution overhang:** INR 16,000 cr enabling approval + history of discounted issuances (PE/SMBC) worries legacy holders.
- **AT1 court case pending** — no provision/adjustment made; adverse outcome is an unquantified tail risk ("if it comes, it comes").
- **NIM path is slow/structural**, not linear, amid intense deposit competition and a rate-cut cycle "on par."
- **SR recoveries lumpy** — timing outside bank's control (JC Flowers).
- **ECL transition + new credit-RWA circular (1 Apr):** some gross P&L impact expected (SR ECL not B/S-allowed), but management "don't expect it to be very material" on core equity.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Measured, credibility-building tone under new-ish CEO Tonse (~5 months in). Repeatedly steered analysts to the *quality* of earnings (core replacing one-offs), was candid that headline 18.3% loan growth overstates the ~15–16% sustainable rate, and clarified the IT-refund one-off is outside NIM. Banodkar precise and conservative on capital/ECL/SR. Handled retail-investor grievances (dividends, CASA, IPO cut-off timing) patiently. No over-promising; NIM/ROA framed as multi-quarter climbs.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The "beat" is really a **mix-quality inflection**: PAT +33.7% *while* SR gains collapsed INR 338→86 cr — the market may under-appreciate that core earnings now stand on their own.
- Reported 18.3% advances growth is partly **transient short-tenor corporate**; the honest run-rate is 15–16% — don't extrapolate the headline.
- IT-refund INR 119 cr is in **other income, not NIM** — so NIM stability (2.7%) is cleaner than a quick read suggests.
- SMBC is shifting from rescuer to **growth engine** (Japan corridor + FCNR limits) — an under-modeled optionality if MOUs convert.
- Enabling capital raise is explicitly **buffer-building near 13% CET-1**, not a distress raise — dilution fear may be overdone, but timing/pricing is the risk.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Capital position remains healthy and supportive of future growth, with CET-I Ratio comfortable at 14.0% v/s. 14.0% in Q1FY26 and 13.8% in Q4FY26"; CRAR 15.1% (v/s 15.3% Q4FY26 and 16.2% Q1FY26), Tier II shown at 1.1% / 1.5% / 2.1%.
- "Key Takeaway: CET 1 at 14.0%, profit-driven accretion, internal accruals & rating upgrades validate capital strength"; the Q-o-Q CET1 walk shows 13.8% Q4FY26, Accretion 0.7%, Consumption -0.5%, 14.0% Q1FY27.
- Stated capital parameters: "RWA/Assets 73.2%, +60 bps YoY"; "+11 bps DTA Q-o-Q Accretion"; "+119 bps CET 1 upside from DTA unwind over time".
- Balance-sheet structure at 30-Jun-26: Shareholders Funds INR 52,338 Crs, Total Capital Funds INR 51,228 Crs, Book Value per share INR 16.7; Borrowings INR 67,940 Crs; Average Quarterly LCR 138.2%.
- Deck discloses no dividend or payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Corporate & Institutional:** strongest grower; but part is transitional/short-tenor, so reported 18.3% overstates the sustainable ~15–16% run-rate.
- **Commercial Banking (MSME):** +17% YoY, high quality, slippages controlled; "very limited impact" from West Asia war on the book.
- **Retail:** book +6.9% (still run-off-dragged from the deliberate 2023–25 slowdown); fresh disbursements 25–30%; multi-product (PL re-accelerating, LAP, franchise home/auto, co-lending); 75:25 secured:unsecured guardrail.
- **Liabilities/Branch Banking:** retail+branch-led ~60% of deposits; best-in-industry cost-of-deposits trajectory over 3 years; FCNR(B) straight deposits flowing well, leverage trade slower.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
> Bank earnings call — mostly firm-specific execution, limited clean sector-reallocation mapping. Kept minimal to avoid padding.

| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| "a Bank of our size like IDFC First Bank is growing CASA very well" (own CASA growth lagging) | **IDFCFIRSTB · 539437 · Private Bank** ⭐ (retail-investor comparison, not mgmt endorsement) | YESBANK (self, on this metric) | Peer cited as running ahead on CASA granularity; **Low** — anecdotal, raised by an investor |
| FCNR(B) leverage-trade slow — overseas FI risk limits + higher global funding spreads gating the flow | SMBC / international banks setting limits (SMBC unlisted in India) | — | Product ramp depends on foreign-bank limit setup; no clean listed Indian beneficiary; **Low** |
> Other call topics (SR-recovery lumpiness, AT1 court case, ECL transition, NIM climb) are internal/regulatory, not sector reallocations — no external listed beneficiary/loser to map.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- "6th Largest Private Bank in India" by Total Assets as on 31st March 2026; "Founded/Licensed in 2003; Commenced operations in 2004"; a "Universal Bank" with a "Comprehensive Product Suite for Retail, Commercial, Corporates & Institutional Segment".
- "Digital Leadership" claim: "Processes every 1 in 3 Digital Transactions in India; Preferred Banker to Unicorns/ Soonicorns; Strong stack of 1,500+ APIs".
- Franchise markers as of Q1FY27: "INR 2.85 Lakh Crs | 69% Loan Book | Share of Retail & Commercial Bank" and "INR 3.15 Lakh Crs | 59% Total Deposits | Share of Retail and Branch Banking led Deposits".
- "Marquee Shareholders SMBC, SBI & Advent"; "29k+ Employees | Senior Management vintage of ~10 Years with the Bank".
- Bank describes itself as offering "Corporate & Institutional Banking, Retail Banking, MSME, Transaction Banking and Treasury", with an International Banking Unit (IBU) at GIFT City and a Representative Office in Abu Dhabi.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Shareholding / SMBC] "Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation ('SMBC') became YES Bank's largest shareholder through the acquisition of 24.9% stake from SBI, other Investor Banks and separately from Carlyle (CA Basque Investments) and others"; "Induction of two SMBC nominee directors" (Mr. Rajeev Veeravalli Kannan, Mr. Shinichiro Nishino); "SBI continues to remain as one of the largest shareholders ... with One Nominee Director on the Board".
- [SMBC scale] "SMBC ... is the 2nd largest banking group in Japan, 14th largest globally; designated as a GSIB, with Total Assets of ~USD 2 trillion"; "SMFG India Credit Company, is one of the largest diversified NBFCs in India, with an AUM of USD 7.0 billion, a customer base of 3 million, and a branch network of 1,015 locations across more than 670 towns". Strategic rationale: "Cross-border Expertise; Access New Business Opportunities - Japanese And Global Corporates" and "Leverage Strong Parentage For Higher Trust".
- [Shareholding pattern 30-Jun-2026] SMBC 24.9%, Resident Individuals 25.4%, FPIs 12.7%, SBI 10.8%, DFIs 10.6%, Verventa Holdings (affiliate of Advent International) 8.5%, Others 4.6%, Other Investor Banks 2.5%.
- [Rating upgrades] Moody's to 'Ba1'/Stable from Ba2 (May'26); S&P Global inaugural 'BB+'/Stable (Jul'26) "establishing a two-agency international profile"; CARE to 'AA+ (Stable)' from 'AA-' (Jun'26); ICRA Infrastructure & Basel III Tier II Bonds to 'AA (Stable)' from 'AA-' (Jul'26); CRISIL AA- from A+ (Aug'25) and India Ratings AA- from A (Aug'25).
- [PSL compliance] "The Bank continues to maintain NIL Shortfall in PSL requirement (overall & subcategories)" and is "On track Ensuring NIL shortfalls in sub-categories by year end"; PSL shortfall deposits INR 27,449 Crs, "lower 25.4% Y-o-Y ... now account for 5.9% of Total Assets".
- [Inclusive banking asset quality] "All new business sourced from 1st January 2025 onward is covered under CGFMU, the Government's credit guarantee scheme. While the overall book has 11.8% NPA (legacy stress accumulated during industry wide credit cycle) the CGFMU book, now 85% of total portfolio, has 1.7% NPA."
- [Security Receipts] Security Receipts under Break up of Investments are "NIL"; the labelled-exposure table separately shows Security Receipts gross INR 3,454 Crs fully provided at INR 3,454 Crs. Management flags "significantly lower P&L Gains from Security Receipts portfolio" - INR 86 Crs in Q1FY27 v/s INR 338 Crs in Q1FY26 and INR 446 Crs in Q4FY26.
- [Normalised metrics] The deck presents pro-forma figures normalised for deposits placed in lieu of PSL shortfalls: NIM 2.7% reported v/s 3.0% normalised; Yield on Interest Bearing Assets 7.9% v/s 8.2%; Cost to Income 62.8% v/s 61.3%; PPOP/Assets 1.5% v/s 1.7%; RoA 0.9% v/s 1.1%; RoE 8.3% v/s 8.9%.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM 2.7% (+20 bps YoY, flat QoQ). Lever = falling cost of deposits (repriced down through FY26/Q1 without deposit attrition) + rundown of low-yield RIDF/PSL deposits + CASA mix, partly offset by rate-cut transmission on yields. Management frames NIM upside as "not too much of a worry."
- Cost-to-income down 430 bps YoY to 62.8% — the clearest operating-leverage signal.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1FY27 (this):** PAT INR 1,071 cr (+33.7%), OP INR 1,704 cr (+25.5%), NII INR 2,786 cr (+17.5%), NIM 2.7% (+20 bps), C/I 62.8%, ROA 0.9%/ROE 8.3%. Advances INR 2.85 L cr (+18.3%; ~15–16% underlying), Deposits INR 3.15 L cr (+14.3%), CASA +14.3%, CET-1 14%, LCR 138.2%. GNPA 1.3%/NNPA 0.2%/PCR 81.7%; retail slippage 10-quarter low. SR gains only INR 86 cr. Rating cluster up: Moody's Ba1, S&P BB+ (inaugural), CARE AA+, ICRA AA. Enabling capital approval INR 16,000 cr. Guidance: loans 15–17%, NIM→3%+ in 2 yrs, ROA ~1% FY27 (+15–20 bps core), SR gains INR 800–1,000 cr FY27, retail double-digit book in 3–4 qtrs, FCNR leverage 9x.
- _next → check: NIM print vs 3% path; core-ROA +15–20 bps tracking; SR gains vs INR 800–1,000 cr; retail book turning to double-digit; whether the enabling capital raise is triggered (price/dilution); AT1 court-case outcome; ECL-transition impact quantified._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Loan growth:** 15–17% (a little above industry); comfortable underlying band 15–16% on avg-balance.
- **NIM:** structural climb to **3%+ handle over next ~2 years** ("north of 3%" targeted by FY28) via RIDF/PSL-deposit rundown, deposit repricing, CASA mix — cautioned it is not linear.
- **ROA:** aspiration of ~**1% full-year reported ROA FY27**; **core ROA +15–20 bps** expansion in FY27.
- **SR gains:** INR **800–1,000 cr for FY27** (JC Flowers-execution dependent, lumpy).
- **Retail:** incremental/fresh business running **25–30%**; book to reach **double-digit growth in ~3–4 quarters**; targeting mid-teens over time.
- **FCNR(B) leverage:** capped at **9x** for now (may revise up on demand).
- **Capital:** enabling approval up to **INR 16,000 cr (~10% dilution)** — optionality only; if used, would raise around the **13% CET-1 handle** to add buffers (not out of need for next 4 quarters).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Banking (no order book): pipeline = retail disbursement momentum (+27.5% YoY; +~30% YoY on disbursements) and FCNR(B)/leverage-trade demand where risk-limit setup with overseas FIs (incl. SMBC) is the gating factor.
- SR resolution pipeline: INR 1,500 cr face value (NAV >INR 2,000 cr) with JC Flowers ARC; corporate-resolution story now "behind us" — future recoveries almost entirely the ARC book.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **SMBC / Indo-Japanese corridor:** MOUs already signed; ambition to route the "max" of India–Japan trade/investment/infra flows (bullet train, shipbuilding, defense-adjacent, Japanese corporates setting up in India) through YES Bank; specifics withheld for confidentiality.
- **FCNR(B) leverage product:** strong demand, limits being built with international banks incl. SMBC — a scalable NRI-flow lever once risk limits are set.
- **DTA cushion:** deferred tax asset lets the bank grow RWA ~12–13% without consuming capital (capital-efficiency optionality).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality
